errors.text: The proposed C/O stabilization mechanism combines evidence from chemically and structurally different alloy families without evidence that ordered oxygen complexes can form or stabilize a dual phase in CoCrFeNi-based alloys.
The cited carbon evidence shows that 0.5 at.% C can convert an FCC+HCP alloy into single-phase FCC, directly undermining the proposed carbon-stabilized dual-phase constitution.
High-energy ball milling followed only by annealing does not provide a defined powder-consolidation step, so the route does not establish that a dense bulk nanocrystalline alloy can be produced.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish OOC or grain-boundary stabilization from ordinary interstitial solid-solution strengthening because it lacks grain-size-matched and phase-fraction-matched controls.
